tactic_checks.rules_sound: `#check @Causal.LadderDual.<n>` on all 40 theorems of Dual.lean (/tmp probe). Every `P_of_dual` is exactly `C.dual.P -> C.P` and every `P_dual` is exactly `C.P -> C.dual.P`, for the 16 two-sided nodes. The Lean names are those of programme/ladder.toml. absolutely_minimal is `Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal C.toPrecausality` reached by dot notation; causally_arc_connected is `CausallyArcConnectedOn ⊤`, so `dual_causallyArcConnectedOn` is used at W := ⊤. Each proof is `.1`/`.2` of the library's iff (Properties, LadderLocal, PushUp, Minimal, ArcConnected, NestedCausalities, NestedConverse); I read the source line of each. The one-sided rules are `C.CausallyOpenFuture -> C.dual.CausallyOpenFuture -> C.CausallyOpen` (causallyOpen_iff is Iff.rfl) and `C.LocallyCausallyOpenFuture -> C.dual.LocallyCausallyOpenFuture -> C.LocallyCausallyOpen` (the definition). No rule concludes a past form from a future form (DEC-163). Probe: `(h : C.LocallyCausallyOpenFuture) ⊢ C.dual.LocallyCausallyOpenFuture` and `(h : C.CausallyOpenFuture) ⊢ C.dual.CausallyOpenFuture` both fail by exhaustive search. The pair rules are `LeNested C C' <-> LeNested C.dual C'.dual` and `CurveNestedOn C C' W <-> CurveNestedOn C.dual C'.dual W` (both reversed, so they are sound). Only `safe forward` attributes are added: no simp, no unfold, no apply rule.

tactic_checks.termination: Mechanism, read in aesop e3cb2f7. A forward pattern rule takes its substitution from `RulePatternIndex.getInGoal`/`getCore` (Index/RulePattern.lean:105-160), which visits the syntactic subterms of every hypothesis and of the target, skipping those with loose bvars. Forward/State/Initial.lean:28-30 and ApplyGoalDiff.lean:39-43 call it, so `P_dual` fires only for a `C` such that `C.dual` is in sight. Probes (/tmp, shipped macro): `COF C ⊢ COF C.dual`, the same with `C.dual.dual.dual`, `C.dual.dual.COF ⊢ C.dual.COF`, the half-lit line's seven facts ⊢ `C.dual.dual.dual.COF`, `LeNested C C' ⊢ LeNested C.dual C'`, and `IsCausal C ⊢ StronglyCausal C.dual` all fail by 'exhaustive search', about 0.3 s each. All 592 negatives of DualExact.lean, rewritten as plain examples (`-DmaxErrors=10000`), give 592 × 'failed to prove the goal after exhaustive search', none at a limit. I took every one of the 78 counterexamples in both orientations, put all of its side-0 truths in context (up to 16 hypotheses) and asked for a side-1 falsity: 67 distinct goals, 67 exhaustive failures. With maxRuleApplications and maxRuleApplicationDepth lifted to 100000, a deep-reversal refuted goal also ends by exhaustion, so the saturation is finite. The control is confirmed: with Rules only, an unpatterned `C.IsCausal -> C.dual.IsCausal` makes `IsCausal C ⊢ Tarentin C` stop at depth 30. Two caveats are recorded as findings 1 and 2: the invariant as written misses the pair rules, and the shipped depth 30 can end a search when a nested reversal is in sight.

docstring: Dual.lean and DualTest.lean each have a title, a prose account of what they cover, a `## SCOPE (disclosed)` section and the provenance line. No labels and no ``**`label`**`` marks (grep `**\``: none), which is correct for a tactic target. The plain bold words (**two-sided**, **Termination.**) are not label marks. The hypothesis checklist does not apply. The SCOPE bullets are true, except for the depth bullet's limitation to conjunctions (finding 2).

findings.what: The termination argument says 'No rule creates a new subterm `t.dual`: `P_dual` writes `t.dual` only for a `t.dual` already present'. That is false for the two pair rules `leNested_dual` and `curveNestedOn_dual`. Their pattern binds only the first causality, and the conclusion also writes `C'.dual`, which need not be in sight. Probe: from `h : LeNested C C'`, `h2 : C'.IsCausal`, `h3 : C.dual.IsCausal` (goal C.Tarentin), the saturated goal contains `fwd_1 : C.dual.LeNested C'.dual` and `fwd_2 : C'.dual.IsCausal`, both new. Termination still holds. A new `t'.dual^k` arises only next to a present `t.dual^k`, so the dual-nesting depth never exceeds what was present and the atoms are finite. Probe: a 3-cycle of LeNested hypotheses with `C.dual.dual.dual` in sight ends by exhaustive search after 20 forward facts. But the argument as written does not prove it.
findings.fix: Restate the invariant in the docstring and REPORT: every subterm the rules write is `a.dual^k` for an atom `a` present and `k` at most the deepest reversal present. The pair rules write `C'.dual^k` only beside a present `C.dual^k`. Alternatively, note the pair-rule exception in SCOPE.

findings.what: The depth bullet presents maxRuleApplicationDepth 30 as a problem of long conjunctions only. It also stops single goals once a nested reversal is in sight in a large context. With the shipped macro and 16 facts of C, the derivable single goals `C.dual.dual.CausallyOpen` and `C.dual.dual.dual.CausallyOpenFuture` fail with 'maximum rule application depth (30) was reached'; at depth 60 the latter closes. A refuted single goal (the half-lit line's seven facts, one stated on C.dual⁴, goal C.dual⁵.CausallyOpenFuture) ends at the depth rather than by exhaustion; at depth 60 it is exhaustive. With 16 facts and seven reversals, aesop also reports the safe-prefix cap (maxSafePrefixRuleApplications, 50). With a single reversal the claim holds in everything I tried: 67 refuted and 36 derivable single goals, in full counterexample contexts of up to 16 hypotheses, behave correctly. All DualTest and DualExact negatives fail by exhaustion. So no shipped test passes for the wrong reason; only the disclosure is too narrow.
findings.fix: Reword the bullet: the depth bounds the saturation, so with a nested reversal (`C.dual.dual`) in sight and many facts a single goal can fail at the depth, derivable or not. For the master's Basic.lean proposal, raise maxSafePrefixRuleApplications together with maxRuleApplicationDepth.

findings.what: The docstring says a goal without a time reversal 'costs what it cost before (the generated tests replay in the same time)'. Nothing is transported, which is true, but the replay is not the same time: Test.lean takes 4.48 s without Dual and 4.77 s with it (mine), and the REPORT itself measures elaboration going from about 3.5 s to 3.7-4.1 s. The extra time is the larger forward index.
